note: 4.3-N3 Amihud: LEGACY prices appear dividend-adjusted; Section 5 normalizes Amihud per fold

finding.statement: LEGACY closes appear to be back-adjusted for dividends. This is an inference, not an established fact.
finding.evidence_in_the_repository: A5 G4: first LEGACY close 62.12 on 2003-01-02; junction ratio 0.99845; the fixed ex-dividend reading rule gave 'inconclusive' (LEGACY gap 0.3061%, RAW gap -0.7405%).
finding.evidence_outside_the_repository: General knowledge, unverified here: SPY traded near 90 in early January 2003; a series adjusted for all dividends up to 2026 would show a much lower level for that date.
finding.consequence: Inference only: if the closes are back-adjusted, the dollar volume (volume x close) in amihud_w is understated in early years and the level of amihud_w drifts with the adjustment factor.
finding.g4_detail: Rule-based reading: inconclusive. Ex-dividend gap in the mean overnight return: LEGACY 0.3061% (SE 0.1233%, 57 sessions, t 2.48); RAW -0.7405% (SE 0.12%, 12 sessions, t -6.17). The two gaps have opposite signs, and the ex-date approximation (third Friday of March, June, September, December) coincides with quarterly options expiration, so this test does not settle the question. Price levels: LEGACY first close 62.12 on 2003-01-02, last TRAIN close 229.57; junction ratio 0.99845 (first RAW Open 431.57 over last LEGACY Close 432.24), a normal one-day move. Inference, not established from the repository: a LEGACY close of about 62 on 2003-01-02, against a level near 90 recalled from general knowledge, and a junction ratio near 1 would both fit closes back-adjusted for dividends up to about March 2022; if so, amihud_w dollar volume is understated in early years. Nothing was changed.
